name: Luna 9
coordinate_accuracy: ±10 km (Telemetric landing ellipse; hardware not unambiguously identified in LROC)
lander_rover_info: E-6 No.13 hermetic instrument sphere (99 kg) with 4 deployable petal antennas

scientific_instruments.name: Television System
scientific_instruments.role: Rotating panoramic telephotometer camera

scientific_instruments.name: SBM-10 Radiation Detector
scientific_instruments.role: Gas-discharge counter measuring cosmic radiation

scientific_observations: First panoramic photographs returned from the surface of another celestial body; proved that lunar regolith possesses mechanical load-bearing capacity (>10 kPa), conclusively disproving the catastrophic dust ocean hypothesis; measured background surface radiation dose of 30 mrad/day.
original_source: Soviet Academy of Sciences (1966) / NASA NSSDCA ID 1966-006A
notes_and_limitations: First survivable soft touchdown on the Moon. Petals deployed 250s after impact cushion landing. Transmitted for 3 days until battery exhaustion.

name: Surveyor 1
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (Sub-meter optical confirmation by LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: Surveyor tripod frame lander with 3 aluminum crushable footpads (294 kg on surface)

scientific_instruments.name: Vidicon Television System
scientific_instruments.role: Variable focus, azimuth/elevation mirror scanning TV system

scientific_instruments.name: Dynamic Strain Gauges
scientific_instruments.role: Measured landing deceleration dynamics and footpad penetration

scientific_observations: First American soft lunar landing; returned 11,237 high-resolution television images; demonstrated surface soil load-bearing capacity of 30-50 kPa, verifying lunar terrain stability for Apollo astronaut landings; monitored lunar surface thermal decline during sunset.
original_source: JPL Technical Report 32-1262 (Surveyor Project Final Report) / Wagner et al. (2017)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Peer-Reviewed Planetary Science
notes_and_limitations: Operated through first lunar night until July 13, 1966. Confirmed smooth mare terrain safety.

name: Luna 13
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 km (Telemetric estimate)
lander_rover_info: E-6M No.205 lander capsule (113 kg) with deployable instrument booms

scientific_instruments.name: Mechanical Penetrometer (PROP)
scientific_instruments.role: Pyrotechnic impulse rod penetrometer measuring soil resistance

scientific_instruments.name: Gamma-Ray Densitometer
scientific_instruments.role: Soil density backscattering measurement probe

scientific_instruments.name: Panoramic TV Cameras
scientific_instruments.role: Twin telephotometer panoramic cameras

scientific_observations: Conducted first in-situ mechanical penetration and radiation density probing of lunar soil; determined regolith bulk density to be 0.8-1.5 g/cm³ and mechanical bearing resistance to 20 cm depth; transmitted 5 distinct panoramic sweeps under changing solar elevation.
original_source: Soviet Academy of Sciences (1967) / Cherkasov et al., Soil Mechanics on the Moon
notes_and_limitations: Operated until December 28, 1966. Proved lunar upper regolith is lightly compacted at the surface and densifies rapidly with depth.

name: Surveyor 3
coordinate_accuracy: ±1 m (Inspected on foot by Apollo 12 crew; LROC NAC M104662862R)
lander_rover_info: Surveyor frame lander with motorized pantograph soil scoop mechanism

scientific_instruments.name: Surface Sampler Mechanism
scientific_instruments.role: Motorized scoop capable of digging trenches up to 18 cm deep

scientific_instruments.name: Vidicon Television System
scientific_instruments.role: Panoramic and surface inspection imaging

scientific_observations: First robotic excavation and trenching of lunar regolith; excavated 4 trenches up to 18 cm deep, testing cohesion and bearing strength; returned 6,315 television images; visited in November 1969 by Apollo 12 astronauts Conrad and Bean, who removed the camera and scoop for terrestrial lab examination (evaluating long-term micro-meteoroid and radiation wear).
original_source: NASA SP-184 (Surveyor 3 Preliminary Science Report) / Apollo 12 Mission Report
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Landed inside a 200m crater on a 12° slope. Bounced twice upon landing due to delayed radar engine cutoff.

name: Surveyor 5
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (Resolved inside 8-meter crater on LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: Surveyor frame lander equipped with alpha-scattering chemical analyzer

scientific_instruments.name: Alpha-Scattering Surface Analyzer
scientific_instruments.role: Curium-242 source measuring alpha particle backscatter and proton reactions

scientific_instruments.name: Television Camera System
scientific_instruments.role: Panoramic high-resolution imaging

scientific_instruments.name: Magnet Assembly
scientific_instruments.role: Magnetic bar on footpad measuring iron content

scientific_observations: Conducted the first in-situ chemical compositional analysis of the Moon; determined mare regolith is volcanic basalt rich in silicon (58-65 atom%), oxygen, aluminum, with ~3% titanium; conducted vernier engine blast firing on the surface to assess rocket plume regolith erosion; returned 19,049 TV frames.
original_source: Turkevich et al. (1968), Science / NASA SP-173
notes_and_limitations: Overcame a critical mid-course helium leak; landed on a 20° slope inside an 8-meter rimless crater in Mare Tranquillitatis.

name: Surveyor 6
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (Resolved with hop depression on LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: Surveyor frame lander with restartable vernier propulsion

scientific_instruments.name: Alpha-Scattering Surface Analyzer
scientific_instruments.role: In-situ elemental chemical analysis

scientific_instruments.name: Television Camera System
scientific_instruments.role: High-resolution panoramic photography

scientific_instruments.name: Magnetic Footpad Bar
scientific_instruments.role: Assessed magnetic mineral concentration

scientific_observations: Confirmed mare basalt composition in central nearside disk; executed first lunar surface liftoff and hop on Nov 17, 1967 (fired engines for 2.5 sec, hopped 2.5 meters away and landed safely), providing stereoscopic imaging of original footprints and evaluating rocket dynamics.
original_source: JPL Technical Report 32-1262 / NASA SP-166
notes_and_limitations: Verified Sinus Medii equatorial candidate corridor for early Apollo missions.

name: Surveyor 7
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (Resolved on rugged Tycho ejecta by LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: Surveyor frame lander with both alpha-scattering analyzer and motorized scoop

scientific_instruments.name: Alpha-Scattering Surface Analyzer
scientific_instruments.role: Highland rock elemental analysis

scientific_instruments.name: Surface Sampler Scoop
scientific_instruments.role: Moved boulders and excavated trenches

scientific_instruments.name: Laser Detector Mirrors
scientific_instruments.role: Detected Earth-based laser pulses (Kitt Peak and Table Mountain)

scientific_observations: Only Surveyor mission sent to rugged highland terrain (Tycho ejecta blanket); discovered that highland rocks are depleted in iron and titanium compared to mare basalts and rich in aluminum and calcium (anorthositic signature); detected laser beams directed from Earth observatories; analyzed rough boulder ejecta field.
original_source: NASA SP-173 / Patterson et al. (1970), Science
notes_and_limitations: Highest southern latitude Surveyor mission (40.86°S). Landed in rocky, bouldery highlands without damaging landing gear.

name: Apollo 11
coordinate_accuracy: ±0.5 m (LROC NAC sub-meter resolution of LM descent stage and equipment)
lander_rover_info: Lunar Module LM-5 'Eagle' (Descent Stage left on surface, 2,034 kg dry)

scientific_instruments.name: Passive Seismic Experiment Package (PSEP)
scientific_instruments.role: Monitored lunar seismicity and meteorite impacts

scientific_instruments.name: Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR)
scientific_instruments.role: 100 corner-cube quartz prisms for sub-centimeter Earth-Moon laser ranging

scientific_instruments.name: Solar Wind Composition (SWC)
scientific_instruments.role: Deployable aluminum foil measuring noble gas isotopic ratios in solar wind

scientific_observations: First human exploration of the lunar surface (Neil Armstrong & Buzz Aldrin); returned 21.55 kg of lunar mare basalts and breccias; dated Mare Tranquillitatis volcanism to ~3.7 billion years; LRRR remains operational after 55+ years, establishing the Moon's orbital recession rate (3.8 cm/yr) and testing General Relativity; detected lunar thermal seismic events.
original_source: Apollo 11 Mission Report (NASA SP-214) / Wagner et al. (2017)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Surface stay time 21.6 hours. Single EVA duration 2h 31m. Astronaut max traverse radius ~60m.

name: Apollo 12
coordinate_accuracy: ±0.5 m (LROC NAC ground truth; 160m from Surveyor 3)
lander_rover_info: LM-6 'Intrepid' Descent Stage, ALSEP central station

scientific_instruments.name: ALSEP Central Station (PSE, LSM, SWS, SIDE, CCIG)
scientific_instruments.role: Long-lived geophysical observatory powered by SNAP-27 RTG

scientific_instruments.name: Solar Wind Spectrometer (SWS)
scientific_instruments.role: Measured solar wind electron and proton energy spectra

scientific_instruments.name: Lunar Surface Magnetometer (LSM)
scientific_instruments.role: Mapped crustal remanent magnetic fields (measured 38 nT field)

scientific_observations: Demonstrated precision landing (~160m from Surveyor 3); Charles Conrad & Alan Bean conducted 2 EVAs (7h 45m); returned 34.35 kg samples including younger mare basalts (3.1-3.3 Ga) and KREEP ejecta from Copernicus crater; retrieved Surveyor 3 parts; ALSEP operated continuously for 8 years transmitting seismic and magnetic data.
original_source: Apollo 12 Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-235)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Surface stay 31.5 hours. First RTG-powered ALSEP station deployed on the Moon.

name: Luna 16
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (Lander descent stage spotted on LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: E-8-5 landing stage + ascent stage with spherical Earth return capsule

scientific_instruments.name: Rotary-Percussion Core Drill
scientific_instruments.role: Drilled to 35 cm depth in darkness before sunrise

scientific_instruments.name: Radiation & Photometer Sensors
scientific_instruments.role: Measured descent dynamics and radiation

scientific_observations: First fully automated robotic sample return from another celestial body; drilled to 35 cm depth and returned 101 grams of core sample to Earth on Sept 24, 1970; chemical analysis confirmed ilmenite-rich basalt with crystallization age ~3.4 Ga.
original_source: Vinogradov (1971), Nature / Soviet Academy of Sciences
notes_and_limitations: Landed in total darkness during lunar night; ascent stage fired automatically back to Kazakhstan.

name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
coordinate_accuracy: ±1 m (Rover parking coordinate: 38.3151°N, -35.0017°W confirmed by LROC)
lander_rover_info: Luna 17 lander stage + Lunokhod 1 eight-wheeled robotic rover (840 kg)

scientific_instruments.name: RIFMA X-ray Fluorescence Spectrometer
scientific_instruments.role: Analyzed regolith chemical composition

scientific_instruments.name: PROP Cone Penetrometer
scientific_instruments.role: Executed 500 mechanical penetrations

scientific_instruments.name: French Laser Retroreflector
scientific_instruments.role: 14 corner-cube silica reflectors for Earth laser ranging

scientific_observations: First planetary robotic roving vehicle; operated for 322 Earth days (planned for 90); traversed 10,540 meters across Mare Imbrium; transmitted 20,000 television frames and 206 high-res panoramas; conducted 500 soil penetrations and 25 X-ray chemical analyses; laser retroreflector rediscovered by LROC and Apache Point Observatory in 2010.
original_source: Soviet Academy of Sciences (1971) / Murphy et al. (2011), Icarus
notes_and_limitations: Operated through 11 lunar nights using polonium-210 radioisotope heater unit.

name: Apollo 14
coordinate_accuracy: ±0.5 m (LROC NAC sub-meter resolution of LM, ALSEP, MET tracks)
lander_rover_info: LM-8 'Antares' Descent Stage, Modular Equipment Transporter (MET pull cart)

scientific_instruments.name: Active Seismic Experiment (ASE)
scientific_instruments.role: Generated seismic waves via thumper and mortar charges

scientific_instruments.name: Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE)
scientific_instruments.role: Long-term monitoring of moonquakes

scientific_instruments.name: Charged Particle Lunar Environment (CPLEE)
scientific_instruments.role: Measured fluxes of solar wind electrons and protons

scientific_instruments.name: Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR)
scientific_instruments.role: Corner-cube laser reflector array

scientific_observations: Alan Shepard & Edgar Mitchell explored the Fra Mauro highlands; returned 42.28 kg samples from Cone Crater ejecta; confirmed Fra Mauro is ancient ejecta from the giant Imbrium basin impact; active seismic thumper determined regolith thickness is 8.5m; collected sample 14321 ('Big Bertha'), containing a terrestrial meteorite fragment formed on Earth ~4.0 Ga.
original_source: Apollo 14 Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-272)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Two EVAs totaling 9h 22m. Shepard hit two golf balls on the lunar surface.

name: Apollo 15
coordinate_accuracy: ±0.5 m (LROC NAC confirmed; LM, LRV, and ALSEP mapped)
lander_rover_info: LM-10 'Falcon' Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1)

scientific_instruments.name: Heat Flow Experiment (HFE)
scientific_instruments.role: Two boreholes measuring internal lunar geothermal heat flux

scientific_instruments.name: Lunar Surface Magnetometer (LSM)
scientific_instruments.role: Mapped local crustal magnetic fields

scientific_instruments.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1)
scientific_instruments.role: First electric roving vehicle on the Moon

scientific_instruments.name: Apollo Lunar Surface Drill
scientific_instruments.role: Extracted 3-meter continuous regolith core

scientific_observations: First extended J-class scientific mission; David Scott & James Irwin traversed 27.9 km in LRV-1 along Hadley Rille and Mt. Hadley Delta; returned 77.31 kg of samples including the famous 'Genesis Rock' (sample 15415, anorthosite dated at ~4.1 Ga, validating the lunar magma ocean hypothesis); first in-situ planetary heat flow measurements (measured heat flux of 21 ± 3 mW/m²).
original_source: Apollo 15 Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-289)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Three EVAs totaling 18h 33m. Demonstrated Galileo's hammer-and-feather gravitational equivalence experiment.

name: Luna 20
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (LROC NAC identified descent stage 1.8 km from Luna 18)
lander_rover_info: E-8-5M robotic lander and ascent return vehicle

scientific_instruments.name: Rotary-Percussion Diamond Drill
scientific_instruments.role: Drilled into hard anorthositic highland rock

scientific_instruments.name: Telephotometer System
scientific_instruments.role: Monitored drilling and surface condition

scientific_observations: First robotic sample return from the lunar highlands; drilled into tough anorthositic rock and returned 55 grams of core sample to Earth on Feb 25, 1972; geochemical analysis demonstrated that the bright lunar terrae (highlands) consist predominantly of anorthosite (rich in plagioclase feldspar), fundamentally distinct from mare basalts.
original_source: Vinogradov (1973), Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta / Soviet Academy of Sciences
notes_and_limitations: Landed only 1.8 km from the impact site of the failed Luna 18 mission.

name: Apollo 16
coordinate_accuracy: ±0.5 m (LROC NAC sub-meter resolution of LM, LRV, ALSEP)
lander_rover_info: LM-11 'Orion' Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-2)

scientific_instruments.name: Far UV Camera/Spectrograph
scientific_instruments.role: First astronomical telescope operated on the lunar surface

scientific_instruments.name: ALSEP (PSE, ASE, LSM, HFE)
scientific_instruments.role: Geophysical observatory suite

scientific_instruments.name: Lunar Portable Magnetometer (LPM)
scientific_instruments.role: Measured localized magnetic anomalies along traverse

scientific_observations: John Young & Charles Duke traversed 26.7 km in LRV-2 across Cayley Plains and Stone Mountain; returned 95.71 kg samples; completely overturned pre-mission theory of highland volcanism by discovering that the Cayley and Descartes formations consist of impact-melt breccias; Far UV camera obtained astronomical spectra of Earth's geocorona, the solar wind, and deep-space nebulae.
original_source: Apollo 16 Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-315)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Highest elevation Apollo landing site (1.4 km above lunar datum). Three EVAs totaling 20h 14m.

name: Apollo 17
coordinate_accuracy: ±0.5 m (LROC NAC sub-meter resolution of LM, LRV, ALSEP, footpaths)
lander_rover_info: LM-12 'Challenger' Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-3)

scientific_instruments.name: Heat Flow Experiment (HFE)
scientific_instruments.role: Measured steady-state lunar heat flow (16 ± 2 mW/m²)

scientific_instruments.name: Traverse Gravimeter (TGE)
scientific_instruments.role: Measured relative gravity differences across valley floor

scientific_instruments.name: Lunar Atmospheric Composition Experiment (LACE)
scientific_instruments.role: Detected noble gases in tenuous exosphere

scientific_instruments.name: Surface Electrical Properties (SEP)
scientific_instruments.role: Interferometric radar mapping of subsurface layering

scientific_observations: Final crewed Apollo mission; Gene Cernan & Harrison 'Jack' Schmitt (first geologist on the Moon) traversed 35.9 km in LRV-3; returned 110.5 kg samples (largest Apollo haul); discovered iconic orange glass beads at Shorty Crater (pyroclastic volcanic fire fountaining from mantle depth ~3.64 Ga); LACE detected tenuous exosphere of helium, neon, and argon-40; HFE measured thermal heat flux of 16 ± 2 mW/m².
original_source: Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report (NASA SP-330)
source_reliability: Authoritative Space Agency / Canonical Ground Truth
notes_and_limitations: Record surface stay of 75 hours and 22h 4m total EVA time. Schmitt remains the only trained scientist to walk on the Moon.

name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
coordinate_accuracy: ±1 m (Rover final parking position at 25.9232°N, 30.9221°E verified by LROC)

scientific_instruments.role: Laser ranging reflector on rover lid

scientific_instruments.name: Visible Astrophotometer
scientific_instruments.role: Measured night sky background sky glow

scientific_observations: Traversed 39.0 km over 4 months across Le Monnier crater floor and into the Fossa Dstraight tectonic fissure (world off-world distance record held until 2014); transmitted 80,000 television frames and 86 panoramic views; mapped sharp crustal magnetic transitions across the mare-highland boundary; laser retroreflector remains active.
original_source: Soviet Academy of Sciences (1973) / Karachevtseva et al. (2013), Icarus
notes_and_limitations: Rover ceased operating in May 1973 after accidentally scooping loose soil from crater wall into radiator, causing thermal overheating.

name: Luna 23
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (LROC NAC imaged lander resting on its side)
lander_rover_info: E-8-5M robotic lander and sample ascent vehicle

scientific_instruments.name: 2.5-meter Deep Rotary Core Drill
scientific_instruments.role: Designed to extract continuous 2.5m core

scientific_instruments.name: Radio Telemetry Transmitters
scientific_instruments.role: Transmitted engineering data for 3 days

scientific_observations: Successfully soft-landed in southern Mare Crisium, but encountered rough slope and tipped onto its side upon touchdown; the drill apparatus was damaged and unable to collect or load core samples into the return capsule; transmitted engineering telemetry for 3 days; identified by LROC NAC only 2.3 km from the successful Luna 24 touchdown site.
original_source: Soviet Academy of Sciences (1974) / Plescia et al. (2012), LPSC
notes_and_limitations: Landed on side. Set the ground truth target for the successful backup mission Luna 24.

name: Luna 24
coordinate_accuracy: ±5 m (Lander descent stage confirmed by LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: E-8-5M robotic lander and sample ascent return capsule

scientific_instruments.name: Earth Return Vehicle
scientific_instruments.role: Autonomous ascent stage

scientific_observations: Final Soviet lunar mission and last surface sample return of the 20th century; successfully drilled to 2.0 meters depth and returned 170.1 grams of stratified core sample to Earth on Aug 22, 1976; geochemical analysis revealed very-low-titanium (VLT) mare basalts; Russian scientists reported detection of trace water (0.1 wt%) in 1978, verified decades later by modern instruments.
original_source: Barsukov et al. (1977), Geokhimiya / Soviet Academy of Sciences
notes_and_limitations: Marked the conclusion of the first lunar exploration era (1959-1976). Landed 2.3 km northeast of Luna 23.

name: Chang'e 3 / Yutu
coordinate_accuracy: ±1 m (Lander and rover tracks clearly mapped by LROC NAC)
lander_rover_info: Chang'e 3 lander + Yutu 'Jade Rabbit' six-wheeled rover (140 kg)

scientific_observations: First soft landing on the Moon in 37 years; discovered an extraordinarily young (~2.5 Ga) high-titanium, olivine-rich basalt; LPR mapped subsurface regolith thickness and underlying basalt flow layering; MUTC conducted continuous long-duration UV astronomy free from atmospheric absorption; lander functioned for over 8 years.

notes_and_limitations: Yutu rover traveled 114m before suffering mechanical wheel drive issue in 2nd lunar night, but continued scientific observations as stationary laboratory.

scientific_observations: First soft landing on the farside of the Moon in human history; relayed all data through Queqiao halo orbit satellite; VNIS identified mantle-derived low-calcium pyroxene and olivine excavated by the ancient SPA impact basin; LPR revealed deep porous regolith layers; conducted radio astronomy shielded from terrestrial electromagnetic pollution; rover active for >5 years.
original_source: Li et al. (2019), Nature / Di et al. (2019), Science China Information Sciences
notes_and_limitations: Yutu-2 rover has traversed over 1.6 km on the lunar farside, surviving more than 60 lunar days.

name: Chang'e 5

scientific_observations: First lunar sample return in 44 years; retrieved 1,731.2 grams of young mare basalts; isotopic radiometric dating revealed an age of 2.03 billion years, proving the Moon remained volcanically active 1 billion years longer than previous Apollo samples indicated; identified hydroxyl/water in apatite minerals (up to 283 ppm); discovered new mineral 'Changesite-(Y)'.
original_source: Che et al. (2021), Science / Li et al. (2021), Nature
notes_and_limitations: Executed autonomous robotic docking in lunar orbit before returning capsule to Inner Mongolia on Dec 16, 2020.

scientific_observations: First successful soft landing in the lunar southern high-latitude region (69.37°S); ChaSTE probe measured steep vertical thermal gradient from +60°C on surface down to -10°C at 8cm depth (proving extraordinary thermal insulating properties of south polar highland regolith); ILSA recorded natural micro-seismic events and rover movement; LIBS and APXS detected unambiguous elemental sulfur (S), iron (Fe), titanium (Ti), aluminum (Al), calcium (Ca), silicon (Si); Vikram performed 40cm surface hop test on Sept 3, 2023; rover traversed 103 meters.

scientific_instruments.name: ILO-X (Commercial)
scientific_instruments.role: Dual lunar cameras for astronomy and lunar horizon

scientific_observations: First commercial spacecraft to achieve a lunar soft landing; first American return to the lunar surface in 52 years; southern-most landing site at the time (80.13°S, ~300 km from South Pole); NDL lidar data proved operational navigation suitability; RFMG validated propellant cryogenic gauging in microgravity.
original_source: NASA CLPS Office / Intuitive Machines Mission Telemetry / LROC Featured Image (IM-1)
notes_and_limitations: Landed with lateral velocity causing one landing leg to catch, resting at ~30° tilt.

name: Chang'e 6
site_name: Apollo Crater, South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin (Statio Tianchuan Farside)
coordinate_accuracy: ±2 m (Confirmed by LRO NAC M1474251740R in southern Apollo basin)
lander_rover_info: Four-module complex with Queqiao-2 relay satellite; drill and robotic arm with mini-rover

scientific_instruments.name: LMS Mineralogical Spectrometer
scientific_instruments.role: In-situ mineralogical spectra of farside sampling area

scientific_instruments.name: DORN (France)
scientific_instruments.role: Detection of Outgassing Radon measuring radioactive gas transport

scientific_instruments.name: NILS (ESA / Sweden)
scientific_instruments.role: Negative Ions at the Lunar Surface detector

scientific_instruments.name: INRRI (Italy)
scientific_instruments.role: Passive laser retroreflector array

scientific_instruments.name: Autonomous Mini-Rover
scientific_instruments.role: Autonomous mobile camera photographing lander and national flag

scientific_observations: First sample return in history from the lunar farside; returned 1,935.3 grams of farside material to Earth on June 25, 2024; sampled ancient farside basalts inside the deep SPA impact basin; DORN measured radon gas transport in farside regolith; mini-rover photographed the lander with national flag deployed.
original_source: CNSA Official Release (June 2024) / Nature / Science China
notes_and_limitations: Historic milestone providing the first direct physical samples of the lunar farside and mantle dichotomy.

scientific_instruments.role: High-precision single large retroreflector

scientific_observations: Planned high-priority subsurface thermal flow investigation (LISTER will drill up to 3m deep to measure heat flow inside Mare Crisium); analyze regolith electrostatics and dust adherence under solar wind bombardment.
original_source: NASA CLPS TO19D Manifest / Firefly Aerospace Mission Portal
notes_and_limitations: 10 NASA-sponsored instruments investigating lunar heat flow, radiation, and regolith dust physics.

scientific_instruments.role: Autonomous rocket hopper designed to fly into a Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR)

scientific_observations: First in-situ volatile and water ice drilling attempt at the extreme Lunar South Pole (Connecting Ridge, 89.45°S); TRIDENT will drill 1 meter down into cryogenic regolith; MSolo mass spectrometer will detect evolving water vapor, CO2, methane, and volatiles; μNova hopper will hop directly into a permanently shadowed region cold trap.
original_source: NASA CLPS Office / Intuitive Machines Mission 2 Plan / Paul et al. (2024)
notes_and_limitations: Premier precursor for Artemis crewed landing site volatile verification.
